findings.passage: I authored this amendment to the Wisconsin Constitution to ensure that the people of Wisconsin have full confidence in the security and integrity of Wisconsin elections. This Joint Resolution would amend the State Constitution to require valid photographic identification when voting. Under the amendment, the State Legislature would still be able to create exceptions to the requirement in statutes and qualified electors who lack valid identification on elections day would still be able to cast a provisional ballot. This proposal does not change any current statutory exceptions to existing voter ID requirements.
findings.note: Written testimony to the Assembly Committee on Campaigns and Elections on AJR 1, a constitutional amendment requiring photo ID to vote; describes the provisional-ballot path and statutory exceptions.
subjects: provisional ballot for voters without ID

findings.passage: Wisconsin's voter ID requirement has been widely successful in preserving election integrity and ensuring that citizens are confident that the ballots cast are legitimate.
findings.note: Same testimony; says the existing voter ID requirement has worked and cites polling support.

findings.passage: “If we wait on something like this, then (the court) could rule that the photo ID is unconstitutional, and then it would be a harder time,” said Rep. Patrick Snyder, R-Weston, the bill’s co-author. “This gives the electorate the opportunity to make that decision.”
findings.note: Quoted by WPR in a story on the photo ID amendment; gives his reason for putting it in the constitution now.
